severity_scale.critical: Consensus, funds or keys at risk.
severity_scale.high: Ingestion halts, or value is attributed to the wrong account.
severity_scale.medium: Data is silently lost or wrong (an amount, an ID, a missing record), or a valid network value is rejected on a common path.
severity_scale.low: A valid but rare value is rejected or mishandled; tooling or test infrastructure is affected.
severity_scale.info: Behaviour worth knowing about that isn't a defect.

findings.title: Ingestion halts on a CAP-40 signed-payload signer
findings.summary: A SetOptions that adds a P… signer produces a state change whose signer column can't be encoded (68-byte key into a 33-byte AddressBytea). The COPY fails, the persist transaction rolls back with the cursor, and ingestion retries the ledger forever.
findings.evidence: Pilot at 2a0a84e (before): dropped, records persist: state_change.SignerAccountID … has a 68-byte key. At 2c87335 (the fix): correct. Protocol 28 corpus, kit/pilot/wallet-backend/refs.json.

findings.title: SAC-created trustlines produce no trustline state change
findings.summary: A trustline created by the Stellar Asset Contract's trust() has no changeTrust operation; an indexer keyed on operation types records the trustline but no TRUSTLINE state change.
findings.evidence: Pilot at 764a4f5 (before): incorrect, TRUSTLINE state change: expected ADD, got none. At c152783 (#734): correct.

findings.title: A Soroban operation from a muxed source halts ingestion
findings.summary: The Soroban participant path added the source as M…, the classic path as G…; both encode to one primary key, the COPY fails with SQLSTATE 23505, and ingestion stops at the ledger. Anyone can trigger it with one cheap ExtendFootprintTtl.
findings.evidence: Pilot at f8e5786 (before): dropped, participants G… and M… encode to the same key. At bb0b162 (#753): correct. istravex-lint IX003 flags the four call sites #753 changed (contract_operations.go:156, 259, 303, 347) at f8e5786 and none at bb0b162.

findings.title: Soroban participants collected by unbounded recursion over the authorization tree
findings.summary: participantsFromInvocationAndSubInvocations recursed over SorobanAuthorizedInvocation with no depth or size limit, and took participants from the authorization tree rather than from what executed. stellar-core bounds neither the tree's depth nor its width beyond the transaction size.
findings.evidence: istravex-lint IX002 flags contract_operations.go:53 at 666a64d and not at 9538b3c, which derives Soroban participants from executed meta. The nested-auth fixture is a real six-level tree from the generated network.

findings.title: Asset issuers and ScMap keys ordered by text instead of network order
findings.summary: Strkeys are base32, where 2–7 sort before A–Z in ASCII but after them in value. 17.2.0 orders issuers by strkey text, so decoding a valid pool-share changeTrust throws ("Assets are not in lexicographic order") and the pool ID can't be computed; scvSortedMap orders keys by their native string forms, which the host rejects.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/js/matrix.mjs: 17.2.0 fails the four checks; 17.2.1 and later pass. The fixture's issuers were chosen so their strkey order is the reverse of their key-byte order; stellar-core accepted the operation.

findings.title: Muxed and offer IDs accept values that encode a different ID
findings.summary: MuxedAccount accepts "0x…" for the maximum ID and id() then returns the string as typed, not the ID the M-address encodes; manageSellOffer rounds a numeric offer ID above 2^53 (9007199254740993 encodes as …992).
findings.evidence: kit/runners/js/matrix.mjs: 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 fail both checks; 17.3.0 and later reject both inputs.

findings.title: scValToNative silently drops map entries whose keys collide
findings.summary: u32 1 and symbol "1" are distinct ScMap keys that become the same object property; the conversion keeps the last and drops the rest with no error.
findings.evidence: On the fixture's real 10-entry map, 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 return 8 entries and no error; 17.3.0 and later throw.

findings.title: XDR string .value getters are lossy for bytes that aren't UTF-8
findings.affected: all versions (documented behaviour since the fix)
findings.summary: The network accepts any 28 bytes as memo text. The SDK's byte-keeping paths (the memo arm's bytes, Memo.fromXDRObject/toXDRObject, TransactionBuilder.fromXDR) keep them; .value decodes leniently and must not be used to rebuild a value.
findings.evidence: All SDK versions pass memo_bytes, memo_class_roundtrip and transaction_roundtrip on a real 28-byte memo containing FF FE, a CESU-8 lone surrogate and a Latin-1 byte.

findings.title: Decoders reserve capacity from untrusted length prefixes and ignore vector maximums
findings.summary: A 12-byte ScVal claiming 2^32 - 1 elements, a 2,000-deep vec, 101 operations and a 29-byte memo must each be rejected cleanly. The corpus keeps them as regression guards: every pinned SDK (JavaScript 17.4.0, go-stellar-sdk 0.9.0, stellar-xdr 30.0.0 with bounded Limits) rejects all five.
findings.evidence: Synthetic fixtures with expect: decode_error; all three runners pass. Not run against pre-fix rs-stellar-xdr releases.

findings.title: Operation meta lists its ledger entry changes in a different order on different runs
findings.affected: 30.0.0 (Homebrew darwin-arm64 build; observed on standalone networks)
findings.summary: Two runs of the same pinned binary on identical input (same keys, transactions and close times) produce identical ledger headers, transaction sets and results, but the LedgerEntryChange entries inside some operations' changes come out in a different order. Anything that hashes or byte-compares meta from two producers (data lake objects from two captive cores, RPC nodes) can disagree on a ledger both closed identically.
findings.evidence: Three generations of the same corpus (node kit/capture/generate.mjs --out …) give identical ledger headers for ledger 20 and three different orders of the pool-share changeTrust operation's eight changes; the first Soroban settings-upgrade transaction shows the same. --check compares metadata order-insensitively (kit/lib/canonical.mjs) and reports when it had to.

findings.title: get-settings-upgrade-txs uses a random salt, so standalone networks can't be reproduced
findings.summary: The upgrade contract is deployed with a random salt, so its contract ID, the upgrade key and every later ledger hash differ between otherwise identical runs. The generator swaps in a seeded salt and re-signs the three transactions.
findings.evidence: kit/capture/drivers/core.mjs, deterministicUpgrade().

findings.title: TransactionBuilder refuses a muxed source or memo on every Soroban transaction
findings.summary: TransactionBuilder throws "Soroban transactions cannot use a muxed source account" (and refuses a muxed operation source or any memo) for every Soroban transaction. stellar-core rejects them only when the single operation is InvokeHostFunction (TransactionFrame::validateSorobanMemo, v30.0.0), so ExtendFootprintTtl and RestoreFootprint with a muxed source or a memo are valid; the fixture is one, accepted by stellar-core 30.0.0. The SDK decodes it but can't build it.
findings.evidence: The generator sets the muxed source on the raw XDR to build the fixture (kit/capture/drivers/core.mjs, rawMuxedSource).

findings.title: Memo text returned as a Go string without UTF-8 validation
findings.summary: utils.Memo returns MEMO_TEXT as a string with no UTF-8 check. Nothing outside tests calls it and no table has a memo column, so it isn't reachable today. Worth a guard before memos are stored.
findings.evidence: istravex-lint IX001 at internal/utils/ingestion_utils.go:17; triaged in kit/pilot/wallet-backend/triage.json.

findings.title: Fee-processing changes over-count Soroban fees
findings.summary: On the fee-bump fixture the fee-processing changes debit 46,340 stroops but FeeCharged is 40,354: the Soroban refund settles after apply. Fees computed from fee-processing balance deltas alone over-report.
findings.evidence: kit/replay/replay.mjs, feeMetaDebit on the reference row.

findings.title: Diagnostic events differ between RPC nodes for the same ledger
findings.summary: The same transaction's meta differed in one diagnostic value (core_metrics invoke_time_nsecs, 188,866 vs 126,592 ns) between two nodes. Diagnostic events are node-local and not consensus data; fixtures re-source meta from canonical ledgers for this reason.
findings.evidence: kit/capture/canonicalize.mjs; the verifier explains a diagnostic-only difference when it sees one.

findings.title: Amounts above 2^53 stroops lose precision in stellar-etl's operation and balance rows
findings.summary: A payment of i64::MAX stroops (922,337,203,685.4775807 units) is exported as amount 922337203685.4775 in the operation row and the trustline balance: float64 columns. The account_credited effect keeps the exact string. Any amount above 900,719,925.4740992 units is rounded the same way.
findings.evidence: kit/pilot/stellar-etl.mjs runs stellar-etl's own transforms over the fixture's canonical ledger: operation details.amount and trustline balance come out 9223372036854775000 stroops, 807 short.

findings.title: A trustline created by SAC trust() produces no trustline_created effect in stellar-etl
findings.summary: The trustline row is exported from the ledger entry change, but the effects transform emits nothing for the SAC trust() call, so consumers of effects under-count trustlines created through contracts. Horizon derives the effect.
findings.evidence: kit/pilot/stellar-etl.mjs: on all three CAP-0073 fixtures, including a real mainnet USDC trust() (ledger 65,212,685), TransformEffect returns no effects for the transaction; TransformTrustline returns the trustline with its i64::MAX limit. Horizon records the trustline_created effect for the same mainnet transaction.

findings.title: Python stellar-sdk's scval.to_native silently drops map entries whose keys collide
findings.summary: String "b" and symbol "b" are distinct ScMap keys that both become the Python key 'b'; to_native keeps the last and drops the string entry with no error. The fixture's real 10-entry map comes back with 9. The JavaScript SDK had the same bug (js-stellar-sdk#1789, fixed in 17.3.0); the Python fix is open as StellarCN/py-stellar-base#1252.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/python/run.py on stellar-sdk 17.0.1: native_keeps_every_entry fails, 9 of 10 entries, no error. Minimal: a two-entry map {string "b": 1, symbol "b": 2} converts to {'b': 2}.

findings.title: java-stellar-sdk orders asset issuers by strkey text and rejects a valid pool share
findings.summary: The same bug as js-stellar-sdk#1766: Asset.compareTo orders same-code assets by their issuers' strkey text, so Transaction.fromEnvelopeXdr throws "Assets are not in lexicographic order" on a valid pool-share changeTrust, and the pool ID can't be computed. Fixed on master by #832, which compares the decoded key bytes, but not in any release.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/java/Run.java on 6.0.0: decode_pool_share_op, asset_compare and pool_id fail on the generated pool-share fixture, which stellar-core accepted.

findings.title: js-stellar-sdk before 17.3.0 cannot decode protocol 30 XDR
findings.summary: Protocol 30 added XDR arms that 17.2.x does not know: StellarValueExt STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS (CAP-0088, millisecond close times) in every protocol 30 ledger header, and ScAddress SC_ADDRESS_TYPE_MUXED_CONTRACT (CAP-0084). js-stellar-sdk 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 reject the whole value ("unknown enum value"). It is an SDK that predates the protocol, not a bug, but an indexer pinned to it stops at the first protocol 30 ledger: testnet has been on protocol 30 since ledger 5,540,313.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/js/matrix.mjs: 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 fail decode on testnet ledger 5,540,402 (header) and on a testnet transaction paying a muxed contract address; 17.3.0 and 17.4.0 decode and re-encode both byte for byte.

findings.title: stellar-php-sdk returns muxed account IDs above 2^63 as negative numbers
findings.summary: A muxed account ID is an unsigned 64-bit integer. MuxedAccount stores it in a PHP int, which is signed, so getId() returns IDs from 2^63 up as negative numbers: 18067157809773112502, the destination of a real mainnet payment, comes back as -379586263936439114. The bytes round-trip, so the M-address is right, but code that reads the ID (an exchange matching a deposit to a customer) gets the wrong one.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/php/run.php on mainnet ledger 65,083,663 (cap27-muxed-payment-pubnet-0002): MuxedAccount::fromMed25519AccountId(...)->getId() is -379586263936439114, expected 18067157809773112502. The other SDKs return the ID exactly.
findings.draft:
**MuxedAccount::getId() returns IDs above 2^63 as negative numbers**

Muxed account IDs are unsigned 64-bit (CAP-0027), but `MuxedAccount` stores the ID in a PHP `int`, which is signed. Any ID from 2^63 up comes back negative.

Reproduction (1.18.0), with the destination of a real mainnet payment (ledger 65083663, tx 1a5e418524e95dd36932533636d96763d28719763bada5a5c31198e1acc01aa7):

```php
$m = MuxedAccount::fromMed25519AccountId("<the payment destination M-address>");
var_dump($m->getId()); // int(-379586263936439114); expected 18067157809773112502
```

The XDR round-trips (the M-address is preserved), so only callers that read the ID are affected, but those are the ones that use muxed accounts: exchanges and custodians matching deposits to customers. A string (or GMP) representation would keep the full range. Found by the Istravex conformance corpus (https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex).

findings.title: stellar-php-sdk decodes values longer than their XDR maximum
findings.summary: XDR bounds variable-length arrays and strings (operations<100>, string text<28>), and a decoder must refuse a value over the bound. The PHP SDK decodes a transaction with 101 operations and a memo text of 29 bytes without error. The network never produces such values, so ledger data is unaffected, but code that parses untrusted envelopes (a SEP-10 challenge, a transaction handed over for signing) accepts what stellar-core would reject. The other SDKs refuse both.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/php/run.php: base-over-max-length-synthetic-0001 envelope_101_ops and envelope_memo_29 decode without error; JavaScript, Go, Rust, Python (both packages) and Java reject them.
findings.draft:
**XDR decoding accepts arrays and strings longer than their declared maximum**

`XdrTransactionEnvelope::fromEnvelopeBase64XdrString` decodes a transaction with 101 operations (`Operation operations<MAX_OPS_PER_TX>`, 100) and one whose memo text is 29 bytes (`string text<28>`). RFC 4506 bounds these, stellar-core rejects them, and the JavaScript, Go, Rust, Python and Java SDKs refuse to decode them.

The two envelopes are in https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/tree/main/corpus/fixtures/base-over-max-length-synthetic-0001 (`envelope_101_ops.xdr.b64`, `envelope_memo_29.xdr.b64`).

Ledger data cannot contain such values, but code that decodes untrusted envelopes (SEP-10 challenges, transactions submitted for co-signing) would accept a value the network never can. Checking the declared maximum in the generated decoders for bounded arrays, strings and opaques would close it.

findings.title: java-stellar-sdk computes the wrong hash for transactions whose PRECOND_V2 fields are all defaults
findings.summary: A transaction can carry PRECOND_V2 with every field at its default (no ledger bounds, no min sequence number, age and gap 0, no extra signers); mainnet has many. Transaction.fromEnvelopeXdr keeps the values but not the arm: TransactionPreconditions.hasV2() is false for defaults, so the SDK re-encodes the transaction as PRECOND_TIME and hashes different bytes. hashHex() returns 035f2643… for mainnet transaction 68f96059…; signing it signs a different transaction. Same root as #837 (the arm is inferred from values), but a different trigger that the fix proposed there does not cover.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/java/Run.java on cap21-precond-v2-defaults-pubnet-0001 (mainnet ledger 59,247,200): tx_hash expected 68f9605938736ef04b390e10807c82105d62ff750d4a6107c259470ab6276ce3, got 035f26438364f74e3c5c8b79ea271c69680faf153e7936c126ad265923e282a0; toEnvelopeXdrBase64() differs from the input. The sweep (.github/workflows/sweep.yml) over 1,001 mainnet ledgers finds 58 of 307,577 transactions whose hash Java gets wrong, every one checked a PRECOND_V2 with all-default fields; Go, JavaScript and Rust hash all 307,577 correctly.
findings.draft:
**A decoded transaction with default-valued PRECOND_V2 re-encodes as PRECOND_TIME, so hashHex() is wrong**

A transaction can use `PRECOND_V2` with every field at its default: no `ledgerBounds`, no `minSeqNum`, `minSeqAge` 0, `minSeqLedgerGap` 0, no `extraSigners`. Mainnet has many, for example 68f9605938736ef04b390e10807c82105d62ff750d4a6107c259470ab6276ce3 (ledger 59247200).

`TransactionPreconditions.fromXdr` keeps the values, but `hasV2()` is false when they are all defaults, so `toXdr()` writes `PRECOND_TIME`. The transaction's bytes change, and so does its hash:

```java
AbstractTransaction tx = AbstractTransaction.fromEnvelopeXdr("<envelope_xdr of 68f96059…>", Network.PUBLIC);
tx.hashHex();               // 035f26438364f74e3c5c8b79ea271c69680faf153e7936c126ad265923e282a0
                            // network: 68f9605938736ef04b390e10807c82105d62ff750d4a6107c259470ab6276ce3
tx.toEnvelopeXdrBase64();   // differs from the input
```

A wallet that decodes such an envelope and signs it signs a different transaction, and an indexer that hashes with the SDK records a hash the network doesn't know. This is the same root as #837 (the arm is inferred from the values), with a different trigger: reading `minSeqLedgerGap` with `longValue()` doesn't fix it. Keeping the decoded discriminant, and re-encoding with it, would.

Found by the Istravex conformance corpus (https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex): JavaScript, Go, Rust and both Python packages hash these transactions correctly.

findings.title: stellar-php-sdk computes the wrong hash for transactions whose PRECOND_V2 fields are all defaults
findings.summary: The same defect as F-0023, in the PHP SDK: a transaction with PRECOND_V2 whose fields are all defaults is rebuilt with PRECOND_TIME, so AbstractTransaction::hash() returns 035f2643… for mainnet transaction 68f96059…. A PHP wallet that decodes such an envelope and signs it signs a different transaction. The XDR classes round-trip the bytes; the high-level Transaction does not.
findings.evidence: kit/runners/php/run.php on cap21-precond-v2-defaults-pubnet-0001 (mainnet ledger 59,247,200): tx_hash expected 68f9605938736ef04b390e10807c82105d62ff750d4a6107c259470ab6276ce3, got 035f26438364f74e3c5c8b79ea271c69680faf153e7936c126ad265923e282a0, the same wrong hash as java-stellar-sdk (F-0023).
findings.draft:
**A decoded transaction with default-valued PRECOND_V2 hashes as PRECOND_TIME**

A transaction can use `PRECOND_V2` with every field at its default: no ledger bounds, no min sequence number, `minSeqAge` 0, `minSeqLedgerGap` 0, no extra signers. Mainnet has many, for example 68f9605938736ef04b390e10807c82105d62ff750d4a6107c259470ab6276ce3 (ledger 59247200).

`AbstractTransaction::fromEnvelopeBase64XdrString(...)->hash(Network::public())` returns 035f26438364f74e3c5c8b79ea271c69680faf153e7936c126ad265923e282a0 for it, not the network's hash, because the rebuilt transaction carries `PRECOND_TIME`. (`XdrTransactionEnvelope` itself round-trips the bytes.) A wallet that decodes such an envelope and signs it signs a different transaction.

Keeping the decoded preconditions discriminant, instead of inferring it from the values, fixes it. java-stellar-sdk has the same defect. Found by the Istravex conformance corpus (https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex).
